## Problem

Nick charges his BYD Shark 6 at a share house on an Athom Smart Plug V3. There is no
way to tell how much of each charge came from the household's excess solar (which would
otherwise have been exported for a feed-in credit) versus grid import, and therefore no
fair, defensible number to reimburse the household. The share house runs a Sungrow
inverter via iSolarCloud, but the WiNet dongle is not currently reachable by Modbus TCP
on the LAN, and it is unknown whether the inverter has a smart meter (i.e. whether HA can
see grid import/export at all). Billing must work today regardless.

## Vision

Nick opens one HA dashboard, sees the car charging in real time, and sees a single dollar
figure — "$X owed this month" — split into solar-diverted kWh (valued at the marginal
feed-in rate the household actually lost) and grid kWh (valued at the consumption tariff).
The number is conservative by construction: whenever solar data is missing, the split
treats the draw as 100% grid, so the household is never undercharged. The moment a solar
export sensor is wired, attribution turns on with a single config change — no rebuild.

## Out of Scope

Native billing integrations or payment collection. Multi-vehicle or multi-plug
attribution. Real-time control of the BYD charger's amperage (the portable charger is
fixed ~10 A). Historical back-fill of charges before this package is installed. Any cloud
dependency other than an optional GoSungrow→MQTT fallback. A Lovelace theme redesign — a
functional dashboard only. Deciding the solar data source: this package parameterises it,
it does not choose it.

## Principles

- Conservative-by-default: unknown solar state resolves to 100% grid so the household is
  never undercharged. This is a hard rule, not a nicety.
- The correct value of solar diverted to the car is opportunity cost — the feed-in credit
  the household forwent — valued at the *marginal* feed-in rate at that instant.
- Billing tolerates ~5 min lag; control does not. Accuracy of the monthly dollar figure
  outranks real-time responsiveness for the billing path.
- Every integral must be immune to sensor dropouts. An `unavailable` reading must never
  inject a spike into a Riemann sum.
- Deterministic before clever: the split, the tier boundary, and the cost are pure
  functions of sensor inputs and adjustable tariff helpers.

## Constraints

- Home Assistant OS, Core 2025.7.3, modern schema (`triggers:`/`conditions:`/`actions:`).
- The plug relay must never rapid-cycle under ~10 A load: any switching automation needs a
  minimum 10-minute dwell in each state.
- Tariffs must be `input_number` helpers, adjustable without editing YAML.
- No secrets in artefacts. Solar source is a single documented entity reference.
- Package must be valid and useful with the solar source absent (grid-only billing).
- The BYD charger is not assumed to auto-resume after power loss until tested; switching
  automation must surface this caveat and stay off until Nick opts in.

## Goal

Deliver a copy-paste HA package (helpers + template sensors + Riemann integrals +
utility_meters + cost sensors + a dashboard, plus a dormant solar-following automation
behind a toggle) that measures BYD charge energy, splits each interval into solar-diverted
and grid kWh using a tiered feed-in valuation, and exposes month-to-date and per-session
dollar costs — working as grid-only billing today and upgrading to full solar attribution
by pointing one setting at a grid-export sensor.

## Criteria

Tariffs and helpers
- [ ] ISC-1: `input_number.tariff_consumption` exists, default 0.24, unit $/kWh, step 0.001.
- [ ] ISC-2: `input_number.tariff_fit_tier1` exists, default 0.08 ($/kWh).
- [ ] ISC-3: `input_number.tariff_fit_tier2` exists, default 0.02 ($/kWh).
- [ ] ISC-4: `input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh` exists, default 8 (kWh/day).
- [ ] ISC-5: `input_boolean.ev_solar_charge_mode` exists (gates the switching automation).
- [ ] ISC-6: `input_boolean.ev_charge_now` exists (manual force-on override).
- [ ] ISC-7: `input_text.ev_grid_export_sensor` (or documented constant) names the grid-export source; absence resolves to 100% grid.

Energy accounting
- [ ] ISC-8: Riemann `sensor.ev_car_energy_kwh` integrates plug power (method left, kWh).
- [ ] ISC-9: `sensor.ev_car_power_w` mirrors the plug power sensor with an availability guard.
- [ ] ISC-10: `sensor.ev_grid_export_w` template reads the configured export source, guarded → 0 when unavailable.
- [ ] ISC-11: `sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w` = min(car_power, grid_export) per the agreed formula.
- [ ] ISC-12: `sensor.ev_grid_to_car_w` = max(0, car_power − solar_to_car).
- [ ] ISC-13: Riemann `sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh` integrates solar_to_car (method left).
- [ ] ISC-14: Riemann `sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh` integrates grid_to_car (method left).

Tiered feed-in valuation

- [ ] ISC-16: `sensor.ev_counterfactual_daily_export` = daily_grid_export + car_solar today (kWh).
- [ ] ISC-17: `sensor.ev_solar_to_car_tier1_w` = solar_to_car while counterfactual < tier1 limit, else 0.
- [ ] ISC-18: `sensor.ev_solar_to_car_tier2_w` = solar_to_car while counterfactual ≥ tier1 limit, else 0.
- [ ] ISC-19: Riemann `sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh` and `sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh` integrate the two tiers.

Utility meters

- [ ] ISC-21: Monthly meters use `cycle: monthly`; daily use `cycle: daily`.

Cost sensors
- [ ] ISC-22: `sensor.ev_cost_month` = tier1_kwh×fit1 + tier2_kwh×fit2 + grid_kwh×consumption (monthly), in $.
- [ ] ISC-23: `sensor.ev_cost_today` = same formula over daily meters, in $.
- [ ] ISC-24: `sensor.ev_session_cost` computes cost for the current/last session.
- [ ] ISC-25: `sensor.ev_session_energy_kwh` accumulates energy since session start.
- [ ] ISC-26: A session starts when plug power > 100 W and ends when it drops below for a debounce window.

Switching automation (dormant — behind toggle)

- [ ] ISC-28: Automation turns plug off when grid import > threshold sustained 10 min.
- [ ] ISC-29: `ev_charge_now` on forces the plug on regardless of solar.
- [ ] ISC-30: Automations use `mode: single` and enforce ≥10-min dwell (no rapid cycling).

Dashboard

- [ ] ISC-32: Dashboard shows month-to-date solar vs grid kWh and $ owed.
- [ ] ISC-33: Dashboard exposes the four tariff inputs and both toggles.
- [ ] ISC-34: Dashboard shows a banner flagging solar-source status and any simplification in effect.

Anti-criteria
- [ ] ISC-35: Anti: a solar-sensor `unavailable`/`unknown` state produces a cost that undercharges the household (must degrade to 100% grid, never 0 cost).
- [ ] ISC-36: Anti: a sensor dropout injects a spike into any Riemann integral (availability templates required).
- [ ] ISC-37: Anti: the switching automation is active with `ev_solar_charge_mode` off.
- [ ] ISC-38: Anti: the package hardcodes a tariff rate anywhere a helper should be read.

- 2026-09-06: Solar source found NOT Modbus-reachable on LAN (only :502 host is a RAK LoRa gateway). Package built solar-source-agnostic with a single documented swap-point and 100%-grid safe degrade, so it ships useful today.

# ============================================================================
# EV Charging Monitor — BYD Shark 6 on Athom Smart Plug V3 (share house)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Home Assistant PACKAGE. Attributes each charge to solar-diverted vs grid,
# and computes a fair reimbursement using tiered feed-in valuation.
#
# INSTALL (HA OS, Core 2025.7.3):
#   1. In configuration.yaml, ensure packages are enabled:
#        homeassistant:
#          packages: !include_dir_named packages
#   2. Copy this file to  /config/packages/ev_charging_monitor.yaml
#   3. Developer Tools > YAML > Check Configuration, then Restart.
#   4. Dashboard: paste ev_charging_dashboard.yaml as a new manual view.
#
# ── TWO THINGS TO SET BEFORE IT'S ACCURATE ──────────────────────────────────
# (A) PLUG ENTITY IDs. Defaults below are the expected ESPHome slugs for
#     node "athom-smart-plug-v3-4cb818". VERIFY in Developer Tools > States by
#     searching "athom" and correcting the four ids in the ANCHORS block if
#     they differ.
# (B) SOLAR / GRID-EXPORT SENSOR. Not yet wired (the Sungrow WiNet dongle was
#     not Modbus-reachable on the LAN at build time). Until you set
#     `grid_export_source` below, the split treats ALL charging as grid, so the
#     household is never undercharged. The dashboard banner shows this state.
#     When solar is wired, set the one line marked  << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>.
# ============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ANCHORS — the only entity ids you should need to touch. YAML anchors keep
# them defined once and reused everywhere below.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plug sensors (VERIFY these four in Developer Tools > States):
#   plug power   : sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_power        (W)
#   plug switch  : switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818
# The templates read these via the names below.

# ===========================================================================
# 1. HELPERS  (ISC-1..7)
# ===========================================================================
input_number:
  tariff_consumption:
    name: Tariff — consumption (grid import)
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:transmission-tower-import
    # default 24 c/kWh flat
  tariff_fit_tier1:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 1
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:solar-power
    # default 8 c/kWh for the first N kWh exported/day
  tariff_fit_tier2:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 2
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:solar-power-variant
    # default 2 c/kWh thereafter
  tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 1 daily limit
    min: 0
    max: 100
    step: 0.5
    unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:gauge

input_boolean:
  ev_solar_charge_mode:
    name: EV solar-following charge mode
    icon: mdi:weather-sunny
    # OFF by default — the switching automation does nothing until this is ON.
  ev_charge_now:
    name: EV charge now (force plug on)
    icon: mdi:flash

# Optional: a visible pointer to the solar source. The templates below use a
# hard constant for robustness (dereferencing input_text is fragile), so this
# helper is display-only unless you wire it into the template yourself.
input_text:
  ev_grid_export_sensor:
    name: EV grid-export source (reference only — edit the template constant)
    max: 120
    icon: mdi:transmission-tower-export

# ===========================================================================
# 2. TEMPLATE SENSORS  (ISC-9..12, 16..18)
#    All carry availability guards so a plug/solar dropout never spikes an
#    integral (returns 0 on unavailable rather than a garbage number).
# ===========================================================================
template:
  - sensor:
      # -- Plug power, mirrored with a guard (ISC-9) --------------------------
      - name: "EV Car Power W"
        unique_id: ev_car_power_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        availability: >
          {{ states('sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_power')
             not in ['unavailable','unknown','none', none] }}
        state: >
          {{ states('sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_power') | float(0) }}

      # -- Grid export, read from the configured source (ISC-10) --------------
      #    << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>  Replace the sensor id on the `set src` line
      #    with your whole-house grid EXPORT power sensor (W, positive when
      #    exporting). While it is missing/unavailable this returns 0, which
      #    forces the split to 100% grid (conservative, ISC-35).
      - name: "EV Grid Export W"
        unique_id: ev_grid_export_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set src = 'sensor.CHANGE_ME_grid_export_power' %}
          {% set v = states(src) %}
          {% if v in ['unavailable','unknown','none', none] %}
            0
          {% else %}
            {{ [v | float(0), 0] | max }}
          {% endif %}

      # -- Split: solar-to-car and grid-to-car (ISC-11, ISC-12) --------------
      - name: "EV Solar To Car W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set car = states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set exp = states('sensor.ev_grid_export_w') | float(0) %}
          {{ [car, exp] | min }}
      - name: "EV Grid To Car W"
        unique_id: ev_grid_to_car_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set car = states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {{ [car - solar, 0] | max }}

      # -- Counterfactual daily export = actual export today + car-solar today
      #    (ISC-16). This is the quantity the FIT tier boundary is measured on:
      #    what the household WOULD have exported if the car hadn't charged.
      - name: "EV Counterfactual Daily Export"
        unique_id: ev_counterfactual_daily_export
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {{ (states('sensor.ev_daily_grid_export') | float(0))
             + (states('sensor.ev_car_solar_daily') | float(0)) }}

      # -- Tier split of solar-to-car power (ISC-17, ISC-18) ------------------
      #    Below the daily tier-1 limit, solar diverted is valued at tier 1;
      #    above it, tier 2. We split the POWER into two buckets and integrate
      #    each, which is exact without a price-varying integral.
      - name: "EV Solar To Car Tier1 W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_tier1_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set cf = states('sensor.ev_counterfactual_daily_export') | float(0) %}
          {% set lim = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh') | float(8) %}
          {{ solar if cf < lim else 0 }}
      - name: "EV Solar To Car Tier2 W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_tier2_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set cf = states('sensor.ev_counterfactual_daily_export') | float(0) %}
          {% set lim = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh') | float(8) %}
          {{ solar if cf >= lim else 0 }}

      # -- Session state machine (ISC-25, ISC-26) ----------------------------
      #    A session is "on" while plug power > 100 W. binary below drives the
      #    session-energy/cost utility_meter reset via automation.
  - binary_sensor:
      - name: "EV Charging Active"
        unique_id: ev_charging_active
        device_class: battery_charging
        delay_on: "00:00:20"     # debounce start
        delay_off: "00:02:00"    # debounce end (BYD taper / brief dropouts)
        state: >
          {{ states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) > 100 }}

# ===========================================================================
# 3. RIEMANN INTEGRALS  (ISC-8, ISC-13, ISC-14, ISC-19)
#    method: left, output kWh. Left-Riemann matches the brief and avoids the
#    trapezoidal over-count on step changes typical of relay loads.
# ===========================================================================
sensor:
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_car_power_w
    name: "EV Car Energy kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_energy_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w
    name: "EV Car Solar kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_grid_to_car_w
    name: "EV Car Grid kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_grid_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_tier1_w
    name: "EV Car Solar Tier1 kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_tier2_w
    name: "EV Car Solar Tier2 kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    round: 3

# ===========================================================================
# 4. UTILITY METERS  (ISC-15, ISC-20, ISC-21)
#    Daily + monthly cycles. The whole-house daily export meter feeds the
#    tiered-FIT counterfactual.
# ===========================================================================
utility_meter:
  # Whole-house grid export, daily — feeds the FIT tier boundary.
  #   << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>  point source at your grid-export ENERGY (kWh)
  #   sensor if you have one; otherwise leave as the template export integrated
  #   below. If you only have export POWER, uncomment the ev_grid_export_energy
  #   integration in section 3-style form. For now this reads a placeholder.
  ev_daily_grid_export:
    source: sensor.CHANGE_ME_grid_export_energy_kwh
    cycle: daily

  # Car energy
  ev_car_energy_daily:   { source: sensor.ev_car_energy_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_energy_monthly: { source: sensor.ev_car_energy_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  # Solar-to-car
  ev_car_solar_daily:    { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_monthly:  { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  # Grid-to-car
  ev_car_grid_daily:     { source: sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_grid_monthly:   { source: sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  # Tier1 / Tier2 solar-to-car
  ev_car_solar_tier1_daily:   { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_tier1_monthly: { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  ev_car_solar_tier2_daily:   { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_tier2_monthly: { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  # Session energy — reset by automation at session start
  ev_session_energy:     { source: sensor.ev_car_energy_kwh, cycle: none }

# ===========================================================================
# 5. COST SENSORS  (ISC-22, ISC-23, ISC-24)
#    cost = tier1_kWh×fit1 + tier2_kWh×fit2 + grid_kWh×consumption
#    All rates read from helpers — no hardcoded tariff anywhere (ISC-38).
# ===========================================================================
template:
  - sensor:
      - name: "EV Cost Month"
        unique_id: ev_cost_month
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        icon: mdi:cash
        state: >
          {% set t1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_monthly')        | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')     | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')     | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption')   | float(0.24) %}
          {{ (t1*r1 + t2*r2 + g*rg) | round(2) }}
      - name: "EV Cost Today"
        unique_id: ev_cost_today
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        icon: mdi:cash-clock
        state: >
          {% set t1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_daily')        | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {{ (t1*r1 + t2*r2 + g*rg) | round(2) }}
      - name: "EV Session Energy kWh"
        unique_id: ev_session_energy_kwh
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: "{{ states('sensor.ev_session_energy') | float(0) | round(3) }}"
      # Session cost uses the current tier mix ratio applied to session energy.
      # Exact per-interval session split would need a per-session integral set;
      # this proportional estimate is accurate when the tariff mix is stable
      # within a session (the common case for an overnight/solar-window charge).
      - name: "EV Session Cost"
        unique_id: ev_session_cost
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        icon: mdi:car-electric
        state: >
          {% set se = states('sensor.ev_session_energy') | float(0) %}
          {% set d_solar1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set d_solar2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set d_grid  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_daily')  | float(0) %}
          {% set d_total = d_solar1 + d_solar2 + d_grid %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {% if d_total > 0 %}
            {% set blended = (d_solar1*r1 + d_solar2*r2 + d_grid*rg) / d_total %}
            {{ (se * blended) | round(2) }}
          {% else %}
            {{ (se * rg) | round(2) }}
          {% endif %}

# ===========================================================================
# 6. AUTOMATIONS
# ===========================================================================
automation:
  # --- Session meter reset at session start (ISC-24, ISC-25) ---------------
  - id: ev_session_reset
    alias: "EV — reset session meter on charge start"
    mode: single
    triggers:

    conditions:

        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_solar_charge_mode
        state: "on"
      - condition: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_charge_now
        state: "off"         # never fight a manual force-on
      - condition: state
        entity_id: switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818
        state: "on"
    actions:
      - action: switch.turn_off
        target: { entity_id: switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818 }

  # --- Manual force-on override (ISC-29) -----------------------------------
  - id: ev_charge_now_force
    alias: "EV — charge now: force plug ON"
    mode: single
    triggers:
      - trigger: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_charge_now
        to: "on"
    actions:
      - action: switch.turn_on
        target: { entity_id: switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818 }

input.content:
# ============================================================================
# EV Charging Monitor — BYD Shark 6 on Athom Smart Plug V3 (share house)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Home Assistant PACKAGE. Attributes each charge to solar-diverted vs grid and
# computes a fair reimbursement using tiered feed-in valuation.
#
# DESIGN NOTES (why it's built this way):
#  * BILLED kWh is anchored to the plug's HARDWARE cumulative energy register,
#    NOT to a Riemann integral. A Wi-Fi/`unavailable` dropout makes HA's
#    integration hold its last value and bill phantom (or zero) charging; the
#    hardware register is monotonic and drift-free. The two Riemann integrals
#    are used ONLY to derive the solar:grid RATIO, which then rescales the
#    hardware total. `sensor.ev_split_residual_kwh` is a health check on that.
#  * Solar diverted to the car is valued at OPPORTUNITY COST — the feed-in
#    credit the household forwent — at the MARGINAL tier active at that instant.
#  * Conservative by default: no solar data ⇒ 100% grid, so the household is
#    never undercharged.
#
# INSTALL (HA OS, Core 2025.7.3):
#   1. configuration.yaml:
#        homeassistant:
#          packages: !include_dir_named packages
#   2. Copy this file to  /config/packages/ev_charging_monitor.yaml
#   3. Developer Tools > YAML > Check Configuration, then Restart.
#   4. Dashboard: add ev_charging_dashboard.yaml as a new view.
#
# ── TWO THINGS TO SET ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# (A) PLUG ENTITY IDs. Defaults below are the expected ESPHome slugs for node
#     "athom-smart-plug-v3-4cb818". VERIFY in Developer Tools > States (search
#     "athom") and correct them here if different:
#        power        : sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_power             (W)
#        total energy : sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy      (kWh, lifetime)
#        switch       : switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818
# (B) SOLAR / GRID sensors. Not yet wired (the Sungrow WiNet dongle was not
#     Modbus-reachable on the LAN at build time). Every line to change is marked
#     << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>. Until then, all charging bills as grid.
#
#     ⚠️ DOUBLE-COUNT WARNING when you wire solar: if your grid-export figure is
#     derived from a mains CT clamp that measures whole-house load, that load
#     ALREADY INCLUDES this plug. You MUST subtract plug power from house load,
#     or `surplus = pv − load` reads ~0 whenever the car charges and you will
#     attribute 100% grid forever. Prefer a true grid-export sensor (Sungrow
#     smart meter, or a CT on the grid tie, not on the house subcircuit).
#     ⚠️ SIGN CONVENTION: `EV Grid Export W` expects POSITIVE when exporting. A
#     single bidirectional meter may report export as negative — invert if so.
# ============================================================================

# ===========================================================================
# 1. HELPERS  (ISC-1..7)
# ===========================================================================
input_number:
  tariff_consumption:
    name: Tariff — consumption (grid import)
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:transmission-tower-import
  tariff_fit_tier1:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 1
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:solar-power
  tariff_fit_tier2:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 2
    min: 0
    max: 2
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "$/kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:solar-power-variant
  tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh:
    name: Tariff — feed-in tier 1 daily limit
    min: 0
    max: 100
    step: 0.5
    unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:gauge
  # Session snapshot anchors (set by automation; not for manual use)
  ev_session_energy_start:
    name: EV session energy start (internal)
    min: 0
    max: 1000000
    step: 0.001
    unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:database-marker
  ev_session_cost_start:
    name: EV session cost start (internal)
    min: 0
    max: 1000000
    step: 0.0001
    unit_of_measurement: "$"
    mode: box
    icon: mdi:database-marker

input_boolean:
  ev_solar_charge_mode:
    name: EV solar-following charge mode
    icon: mdi:weather-sunny
  ev_charge_now:
    name: EV charge now (force plug on)
    icon: mdi:flash

# Display-only pointer to the solar source. Templates use hard constants for
# robustness (dereferencing input_text is fragile), so editing this does NOT
# change behaviour — edit the << SET SOLAR SOURCE >> lines instead.
input_text:
  ev_grid_export_sensor:
    name: EV grid-export source (reference only)
    max: 120
    icon: mdi:transmission-tower-export

# ===========================================================================
# 2. TEMPLATE SENSORS + BINARY SENSOR
#    (ISC-9..12, 16..18, 22..25) — one `template:` block (HA forbids two).
#    Availability guards keep dropouts out of the integrals (ISC-36).
# ===========================================================================
template:
  - sensor:
      # -- Plug power, mirrored with a guard (ISC-9) --------------------------
      - name: "EV Car Power W"
        unique_id: ev_car_power_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        availability: >
          {{ states('sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_power')
             not in ['unavailable','unknown','none', none] }}
        state: >
          {{ states('sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_power') | float(0) }}

      # -- Grid export, from the configured source (ISC-10) -------------------
      #    << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>  replace the `set src` sensor with your
      #    grid-EXPORT power sensor (W, positive when exporting). Missing ⇒ 0 ⇒
      #    split forces 100% grid (conservative, ISC-35). Read the DOUBLE-COUNT
      #    and SIGN warnings in the header before wiring.
      - name: "EV Grid Export W"
        unique_id: ev_grid_export_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set src = 'sensor.CHANGE_ME_grid_export_power' %}
          {% set v = states(src) %}
          {% if v in ['unavailable','unknown','none', none] %}
            0
          {% else %}
            {{ [v | float(0), 0] | max }}
          {% endif %}

      # -- Split: solar-to-car / grid-to-car (ISC-11, ISC-12) ----------------
      - name: "EV Solar To Car W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set car = states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set exp = states('sensor.ev_grid_export_w') | float(0) %}
          {{ [car, exp] | min }}
      - name: "EV Grid To Car W"
        unique_id: ev_grid_to_car_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set car = states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {{ [car - solar, 0] | max }}

      # -- Counterfactual RUNNING daily export = actual export today +
      #    car-solar today (ISC-16). This is the running cumulative the FIT tier
      #    boundary is measured against. Both terms are monotone within the day,
      #    so the tier flag latches once and the two-bucket split equals the
      #    price-varying integral (advisor-confirmed).
      #    << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>  (optional) if you have a daily export CAP
      #    (inverter/network export limit or a daily FIT volume cap beyond which
      #    the rate is $0), clamp with min(..., cap) so capped solar isn't
      #    valued as if it could have been exported.
      - name: "EV Counterfactual Daily Export"
        unique_id: ev_counterfactual_daily_export
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {{ (states('sensor.ev_daily_grid_export') | float(0))
             + (states('sensor.ev_car_solar_daily') | float(0)) }}

      # -- Tier split of solar-to-car power (ISC-17, ISC-18) ------------------
      - name: "EV Solar To Car Tier1 W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_tier1_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set cf = states('sensor.ev_counterfactual_daily_export') | float(0) %}
          {% set lim = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh') | float(8) %}
          {{ solar if cf < lim else 0 }}
      - name: "EV Solar To Car Tier2 W"
        unique_id: ev_solar_to_car_tier2_w
        unit_of_measurement: "W"
        device_class: power
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set solar = states('sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w') | float(0) %}
          {% set cf = states('sensor.ev_counterfactual_daily_export') | float(0) %}
          {% set lim = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh') | float(8) %}
          {{ solar if cf >= lim else 0 }}

      # -- Health check: hardware total vs sum of split integrals -------------
      #    Should track ~0. A growing residual means a dropout is skewing the
      #    integral-derived ratio (the billed $ is still safe — it's anchored to
      #    hardware — but the split may be off).
      - name: "EV Split Residual kWh"
        unique_id: ev_split_residual_kwh
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: measurement
        state: >
          {% set hw = states('sensor.ev_car_energy_int_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {% set s = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {% set g = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {{ (hw - (s + g)) | round(3) }}

      # -- Hardware-anchored billed split, MONTH (ISC-22 inputs) -------------
      #    billed total (hardware) rescaled by the integral-derived ratio.
      - name: "EV Solar kWh Month"
        unique_id: ev_solar_kwh_month
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {% set total = states('sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set s = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set g = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {{ (total * (s / d) if d > 0 else 0) | round(3) }}
      - name: "EV Grid kWh Month"
        unique_id: ev_grid_kwh_month
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {% set total = states('sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set s = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set g = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {{ (total * (g / d) if d > 0 else total) | round(3) }}

      # -- Cost sensors (ISC-22, ISC-23) -------------------------------------
      #    cost = billed_tier1×fit1 + billed_tier2×fit2 + billed_grid×consump.
      #    Billed portions = hardware total × integral-derived fractions. No
      #    hardcoded tariff anywhere (ISC-38). Unit chain: kWh × $/kWh = $.
      - name: "EV Cost Month"
        unique_id: ev_cost_month
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total
        icon: mdi:cash
        state: >
          {% set total = states('sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set s  = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_monthly')  | float(0) %}
          {% set t1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_monthly') | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {% set solar_frac = (s / d) if d > 0 else 0 %}
          {% set billed_solar = total * solar_frac %}
          {% set billed_grid  = total * (1 - solar_frac) %}
          {% set ts = t1 + t2 %}
          {% set t1_frac = (t1 / ts) if ts > 0 else 0 %}
          {{ (billed_solar * t1_frac * r1
              + billed_solar * (1 - t1_frac) * r2
              + billed_grid * rg) | round(2) }}
      - name: "EV Cost Today"
        unique_id: ev_cost_today
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total
        icon: mdi:cash-clock
        state: >
          {% set total = states('sensor.ev_billed_energy_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set s  = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_daily')  | float(0) %}
          {% set t1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_daily') | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {% set d = s + g %}
          {% set solar_frac = (s / d) if d > 0 else 0 %}
          {% set billed_solar = total * solar_frac %}
          {% set billed_grid  = total * (1 - solar_frac) %}
          {% set ts = t1 + t2 %}
          {% set t1_frac = (t1 / ts) if ts > 0 else 0 %}
          {{ (billed_solar * t1_frac * r1
              + billed_solar * (1 - t1_frac) * r2
              + billed_grid * rg) | round(2) }}

      # -- Cumulative (all-time) $ — drives session cost by snapshot diff -----
      #    Uses the all-time integrals (which never reset), so a session that
      #    straddles midnight or crosses the FIT tier is handled exactly.
      - name: "EV Cost Cumulative"
        unique_id: ev_cost_cumulative
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total_increasing
        state: >
          {% set t1 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {% set t2 = states('sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh') | float(0) %}
          {% set g  = states('sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh')        | float(0) %}
          {% set r1 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1')   | float(0.08) %}
          {% set r2 = states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier2')   | float(0.02) %}
          {% set rg = states('input_number.tariff_consumption') | float(0.24) %}
          {{ (t1*r1 + t2*r2 + g*rg) | round(4) }}

      # -- Session energy & cost by snapshot differencing (ISC-24, ISC-25) ---
      - name: "EV Session Energy kWh"
        unique_id: ev_session_energy_kwh
        unit_of_measurement: "kWh"
        device_class: energy
        state_class: total
        state: >
          {% set now = states('sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy') | float(0) %}
          {% set start = states('input_number.ev_session_energy_start') | float(0) %}
          {{ [now - start, 0] | max | round(3) }}
      - name: "EV Session Cost"
        unique_id: ev_session_cost
        unit_of_measurement: "$"
        device_class: monetary
        state_class: total
        icon: mdi:car-electric
        state: >
          {% set now = states('sensor.ev_cost_cumulative') | float(0) %}
          {% set start = states('input_number.ev_session_cost_start') | float(0) %}
          {{ [now - start, 0] | max | round(2) }}

  - binary_sensor:
      # -- Session state (ISC-26) — debounced ---------------------------------
      - name: "EV Charging Active"
        unique_id: ev_charging_active
        device_class: battery_charging
        delay_on: "00:00:20"     # debounce start
        delay_off: "00:02:00"    # debounce end (BYD taper / brief dropouts)
        state: >
          {{ states('sensor.ev_car_power_w') | float(0) > 100 }}

# ===========================================================================
# 3. RIEMANN INTEGRALS  (ISC-8, ISC-13, ISC-14, ISC-19)
#    method: left, kWh. max_sub_interval advances the integral on a timer so a
#    frozen source doesn't silently stall it (advisor hardening). These drive
#    the solar:grid RATIO; billed kWh comes from the hardware register (§4).
# ===========================================================================
sensor:
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_car_power_w
    name: "EV Car Energy Int kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_energy_int_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w
    name: "EV Car Solar kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_grid_to_car_w
    name: "EV Car Grid kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_grid_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_tier1_w
    name: "EV Car Solar Tier1 kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3
  - platform: integration
    source: sensor.ev_solar_to_car_tier2_w
    name: "EV Car Solar Tier2 kWh"
    unique_id: ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh
    unit_prefix: k
    unit_time: h
    method: left
    max_sub_interval: "00:00:30"
    round: 3

# ===========================================================================
# 4. UTILITY METERS  (ISC-15, ISC-20, ISC-21)
#    Daily + monthly. Billed energy is metered off the plug's HARDWARE total
#    (drift-free). The integral meters below feed the solar:grid ratio only.
#    NOTE: monthly meters reset on the 1st — this is for Nick's own accounting,
#    not aligned to the retailer's billing period.
# ===========================================================================
utility_meter:
  # Billed energy — HARDWARE register (source of truth for kWh billed)
  ev_billed_energy_daily:   { source: sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy, cycle: daily }
  ev_billed_energy_monthly: { source: sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy, cycle: monthly }

  # Whole-house grid export, daily — feeds the FIT tier boundary.
  #   << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>  point at your grid-export ENERGY (kWh) sensor.
  #   Absent ⇒ unavailable ⇒ counterfactual falls back to car-solar only.
  ev_daily_grid_export:
    source: sensor.CHANGE_ME_grid_export_energy_kwh
    cycle: daily

  # Integral-derived ratio meters (NOT billed directly)
  ev_car_solar_daily:    { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_monthly:  { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  ev_car_grid_daily:     { source: sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_grid_monthly:   { source: sensor.ev_car_grid_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  ev_car_solar_tier1_daily:   { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_tier1_monthly: { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier1_kwh, cycle: monthly }
  ev_car_solar_tier2_daily:   { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh, cycle: daily }
  ev_car_solar_tier2_monthly: { source: sensor.ev_car_solar_tier2_kwh, cycle: monthly }

# ===========================================================================
# 5. COST SENSORS  — defined inside the single `template:` block in §2
#    (HA forbids two top-level `template:` keys in one package file).
# ===========================================================================

# ===========================================================================
# 6. AUTOMATIONS
# ===========================================================================
automation:
  # --- Session snapshot on charge start (ISC-24, ISC-25) -------------------
  # Records the hardware-energy and cumulative-cost anchors; the session
  # sensors read the difference from "now".
  - id: ev_session_snapshot
    alias: "EV — snapshot session anchors on charge start"
    mode: single
    triggers:
      - trigger: state
        entity_id: binary_sensor.ev_charging_active
        from: "off"
        to: "on"
    actions:
      - action: input_number.set_value
        target: { entity_id: input_number.ev_session_energy_start }
        data:
          value: "{{ states('sensor.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818_total_energy') | float(0) }}"
      - action: input_number.set_value
        target: { entity_id: input_number.ev_session_cost_start }
        data:
          value: "{{ states('sensor.ev_cost_cumulative') | float(0) }}"

  # --- Solar-following: turn ON (ISC-27, ISC-30) ---------------------------
  # DORMANT: initial_state false + gated on ev_solar_charge_mode. Requires
  # sustained export for 10 min (dwell) so the relay never chatters.
  #   << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>  set numeric_state entity to your grid-export
  #   power sensor (W). Left as the template export sensor so it stays valid.
  - id: ev_solar_follow_on
    alias: "EV — solar follow: turn plug ON"
    mode: single
    initial_state: false
    triggers:
      - trigger: numeric_state
        entity_id: sensor.ev_grid_export_w
        above: 2300
        for: "00:10:00"
    conditions:
      - condition: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_solar_charge_mode
        state: "on"
      - condition: state
        entity_id: switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818
        state: "off"
    actions:
      - action: switch.turn_on
        target: { entity_id: switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818 }

  # --- Solar-following: turn OFF (ISC-28, ISC-30) --------------------------
  # Deadband vs the ON trigger prevents oscillation; 10-min dwell enforced.
  #   << SET SOLAR SOURCE >>  set entity to your grid-IMPORT power sensor (W).
  - id: ev_solar_follow_off
    alias: "EV — solar follow: turn plug OFF"
    mode: single
    initial_state: false
    triggers:
      - trigger: numeric_state
        entity_id: sensor.CHANGE_ME_grid_import_power
        above: 300           # import threshold (W) — adjust to taste
        for: "00:10:00"
    conditions:
      - condition: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_solar_charge_mode
        state: "on"
      - condition: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_charge_now
        state: "off"         # never fight a manual force-on
      - condition: state
        entity_id: switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818
        state: "on"
    actions:
      - action: switch.turn_off
        target: { entity_id: switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818 }

  # --- Manual force-on override (ISC-29) -----------------------------------
  - id: ev_charge_now_force
    alias: "EV — charge now: force plug ON"
    mode: single
    triggers:
      - trigger: state
        entity_id: input_boolean.ev_charge_now
        to: "on"
    actions:
      - action: switch.turn_on
        target: { entity_id: switch.athom_smart_plug_v3_4cb818 }

views:
  - title: EV Charging
    path: ev-charging
    icon: mdi:car-electric
    cards:
      # --- Status banner: solar source + any simplification (ISC-34) --------
      - type: markdown
        content: >
          ### BYD charge — fair-share billing

          {% if states('sensor.CHANGE_ME_grid_export_power') in
                ['unavailable','unknown','none', none] %}
          ⚠️ **Solar source not wired** — every charge is billed as **100% grid**
          (conservative). Set the grid-export sensor in
          `ev_charging_monitor.yaml` to enable solar attribution.
          {% else %}
          ✅ Solar attribution active. Feed-in valued at the **marginal** tier:
          tier 1 below {{ states('input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh') }} kWh
          exported/day, tier 2 above.
          {% endif %}

      - type: entities
        title: Now

          - entity: sensor.ev_car_power_w

          - entity: binary_sensor.ev_charging_active
            name: Charging
          - entity: sensor.ev_session_energy_kwh
            name: This session — energy
          - entity: sensor.ev_session_cost
            name: This session — cost
          - entity: switch.athom_plug_v3_4cb818_switch
            name: Plug

        title: Month to date

          - entity: sensor.ev_cost_month
            name: Owed this month
          - entity: sensor.ev_billed_energy_monthly
            name: Total kWh
          - entity: sensor.ev_solar_kwh_month
            name: Solar kWh
          - entity: sensor.ev_grid_kwh_month
            name: Grid kWh

        title: Today
        entities:
          - entity: sensor.ev_cost_today

          - entity: sensor.ev_billed_energy_daily

      - type: entities
        title: Controls
        entities:
          - entity: input_boolean.ev_solar_charge_mode
            name: Solar-following mode (automation)
          - entity: input_boolean.ev_charge_now
            name: Charge now (force on)

      - type: entities
        title: Tariffs (adjustable)
        entities:
          - entity: input_number.tariff_consumption
            name: Consumption (import)
          - entity: input_number.tariff_fit_tier1
            name: Feed-in tier 1
          - entity: input_number.tariff_fit_tier2
            name: Feed-in tier 2
          - entity: input_number.tariff_fit_tier1_limit_kwh
            name: Tier 1 daily limit

        hours_to_show: 24
        entities:
          - sensor.ev_car_power_w
          - sensor.ev_solar_to_car_w
